_README: Ledger of THESES harvested from saved content, as distinct from tips. A tip hands you a ticker. A thesis hands you a structural claim that implies a basket, and the missing work is figuring out what actually expresses it. Every thesis here is UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS under the dashboard's evidence tiering: a structural argument beats a tip and is still not a backtest.

theses.title: Robotics supply chain, the bottleneck under the robot makers
theses.structural_claim: Artificial intelligence supplies the brain for humanoid robots, but the body (actuators, reducers, magnets) is the constrained layer. So the capital opportunity sits underneath the robot makers rather than in them. This is the picks-and-shovels frame that worked for the semiconductor buildout.
what_must_be_true: Actuation really is the dominant share of a humanoid's bill of materials, not a minor line
That share is supplied by a concentrated set of firms rather than commoditised
Humanoid volumes actually scale, since a bottleneck with no throughput is not a market
The bottleneck firms are reachable and tradeable by a United States retail account

load_bearing_claim.claim: 70% of a humanoid robot's cost is actuators
load_bearing_claim.checked_against: Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and Interact Analysis bill-of-materials estimates
load_bearing_claim.note: Published estimates put joint actuators at roughly 30% to 56% of the bill of materials: Morgan Stanley about 56%, Interact Analysis above 30% on high-configuration humanoids and above 50% on simpler ones. Bank of America splits linear actuators at 27% and rotary at 24%, which is about 51% before dexterous hands at 19%. Add the hands, which are themselves actuator-dense, and you reach roughly 70%. So the video's number is defensible ONLY under the broadest definition of actuation and is high against the common one. The thesis does not depend on 70%: it depends on actuation being the largest single cost centre, and that is well supported at any of these figures.

named_companies.name: Sanhua Intelligent Controls
named_companies.us_access: NONE. No United States American Depositary Receipt. Hong Kong 2050.HK or Shenzhen 002050.SZ only, so it needs a brokerage with Hong Kong access.

named_companies.name: Harmonic Drive Systems
named_companies.us_access: HSYDF on the United States over-the-counter Pink market. Exists, but see the tradability gate: it is effectively untradeable at size.

named_companies.name: MP Materials
named_companies.claim: humanoids need 2x to 3x the magnetic material of an electric vehicle

theses.marker_note: Claims $1,000 in SanDisk a year ago is $34,180 today, roughly 34x, with no supporting data and nothing at all on the robotics names' actual performance. Decoration, not evidence.
theses.expression_note: The named companies plus the sector exchange-traded funds the video never mentions, which are the obvious retail expression of a supply-chain thesis and therefore have to be checked rather than assumed.

fund_check.source: Global X issuer file, botz_full-holdings_20260904.csv, 66 holdings summing to 100.04%
fund_check.headline: BOTZ holds NONE of the three named bottleneck companies.
detail: Harmonic Drive: NOT HELD. Sanhua: NOT HELD. MP Materials: NOT HELD.

Layer split by my classification, which is a judgement call and open to argument: about 53% sits in body and component names, about 27% in the brain and robot-maker layer the thesis says to avoid, and about 20% is neither.

The 53% overstates alignment with the HUMANOID bottleneck. Keyence, ABB, Fanuc, SMC, Daifuku, Omron and Yaskawa are factory-automation incumbents, which is a different business from humanoid actuators and reducers. The fund gives industrial automation, not the constrained layer the argument identifies.
NVIDIA is the second largest holding at 10.11%, so the single biggest single-name bet inside a supply-chain fund is the brain layer the thesis argues against.

ARKQ and ROBO were NOT confirmed from issuer files: the ARK and ROBO Global holdings endpoints did not resolve at the URLs tried, so those two rest on a free-feed top-ten only and their full books remain unverified.

theses.title: Water funds as an artificial-intelligence datacentre hedge
theses.structural_claim: Artificial intelligence datacentres consume large amounts of water, water scarcity worsens, therefore water-sector funds are a hedge on the buildout.
what_must_be_true: Datacentre water use is material relative to total demand, not a rounding error beside agriculture and power
Water utilities and infrastructure capture that demand rather than absorbing it as regulated cost
The listed funds actually hold the businesses that would benefit

load_bearing_claim.claim: About 519 millilitres of water per GPT-4 email, per the Washington Post and University of California Riverside
load_bearing_claim.checked_against: Shaolei Ren, University of California Riverside, the researcher who produced the original figure
load_bearing_claim.note: The 519ml figure traces to the 2023 'Making AI Less Thirsty' study on GPT-3-era inference. Ren has since revised it to roughly 15ml full scope per GPT-4-class prompt, about 5ml counting only the datacentre, and stated the original was time-specific and assumption-based and should not be used to describe today's optimised systems. OpenAI puts an average query near 0.3ml. The gap is partly definitional, since the original counted water evaporated at power plants and modelled a coal-heavy 2023 Iowa grid, but the video presents a superseded number as current and the revision is roughly 35x. The supporting map is the OECD Environmental Outlook from 2008 projecting 2030, an eighteen-year-old projection presented without noting newer work exists.

theses.marker_note: Cites a real source, which is what made the retraction findable. That is better than an unsourced claim.
theses.expression_note: Downgrade the thesis, do not discard the instruments. Water scarcity is a genuine long-horizon theme and these are ordinary, liquid exchange-traded funds. What does not survive is the specific artificial-intelligence urgency, which rested on the retracted figure.

theses.title: Pre-IPO proxy exposure to Anthropic and SpaceX
theses.creator: Michael Sikand (sikandinvests)
theses.structural_claim: Anthropic and SpaceX are heading for enormous initial public offerings. You cannot buy either directly, so the trade is to own listed companies that already have contractual revenue from them or hold equity in them, and be positioned before the listing repricing.
what_must_be_true: The initial public offerings actually happen, and on a horizon worth waiting for
The proxy link is material to the proxy company, not a rounding error on its revenue
The market has not already priced the link, which is the weak point since every deal here was announced months ago and moved the stock on the day
The proxy company's own business does not swamp the exposure you are buying

load_bearing_claim.claim: Three listed companies have real, large Anthropic exposure
load_bearing_claim.verdict: ALL THREE VERIFIED, which is a first for this batch
load_bearing_claim.checked_against: Bloomberg, Reuters, Data Center Dynamics, company reporting
load_bearing_claim.note: Riot Platforms: VERIFIED and LARGER than the video said. A real 9.1 billion dollar, 191 megawatt, 20-year lease at the Rockdale Texas campus running through June 2048, announced August 2026, worth up to 16.1 billion with two five-year extensions. Akamai: VERIFIED. A 1.8 billion dollar seven-year cloud deal announced 8 May 2026, the largest in Akamai's history; revenue starts in the fourth quarter of 2026 at about 20 to 25 million dollars. SK Telecom: VERIFIED in substance. It invested about 270 billion won since 2023 and the stake was carried above 3.5 trillion won, roughly 2.5 billion dollars, at the end of June, and it joined the 65 billion dollar Series H at a 965 billion post-money valuation. The 2 trillion dollar initial public offering figure is a QUESTION, not a fact: the video's own source graphic carries a question mark, and the last marked round was 965 billion.

named_companies.name: Riot Platforms (RIOT)
named_companies.claim: Anthropic contract; market capitalisation only 8 billion
named_companies.verdict: VERIFIED, and the deal is bigger than stated

named_companies.name: Akamai Technologies (AKAM)
named_companies.claim: 1.8 billion dollar Anthropic deal; trading at just 15 times
named_companies.verdict: DEAL VERIFIED. The multiple is the forward one (14.9x); trailing price to earnings is 38.8x, so quoting 15 flatters it

named_companies.name: SK Telecom (SKM)
named_companies.role: holds Anthropic EQUITY, not a contract
named_companies.claim: the closest thing to a pure play equity on Anthropic
named_companies.verdict: DEFENSIBLE ON THE NUMBERS, wrong on the words
named_companies.us_access: NYSE American Depositary Receipt, ordinary access.

theses.marker_note: Notably better sourced than the earlier batch: every factual claim it makes checks out against real reporting, and it names its source graphics. It still ends on a subscription promotion for the creator's own portfolio product and discloses no position, and it gives no entry, exit or sizing.
theses.expression_note: The three the video names, plus the two it SHOWS AND THEN IGNORES. Its own ownership pie chart puts Amazon at 17 percent and Google at 14 percent, far larger holders than SK Telecom, and it picks neither.

fund_check.source: Anthropic marked at 965 billion post-money (Series H); market capitalisations live from yfinance
fund_check.headline: How much Anthropic you actually get per dollar, which is the comparison the video skips.
detail: SK Telecom: about 14 billion market capitalisation against an implied 3 billion stake, so roughly 20 percent of the company is the Anthropic position. Amazon: 6.0 percent. Alphabet: 3.3 percent.

So 'closest thing to a pure play' is DEFENSIBLE on the ratio that matters, even though 'pure play' is the wrong phrase for a Korean telecom whose main business is mobile service. Call it the most concentrated liquid exposure, not a pure play.
The Amazon and Alphabet percentages are CONTENT-SOURCED from the video's pie chart and are not independently verified. SK Telecom's is verified from reporting.

Dilution is the live risk on the SK Telecom line: the stake went from about 2 percent at entry to about 0.3 percent after later rounds. Each new raise marks the value up and the ownership down, so the exposure erodes even as the headline number grows.

The market-priced-it objection is the strongest one against the whole thesis. Every deal here was announced months ago and moved the stock hard on the day: Akamai closed up 27 percent at 148.38 dollars on its announcement and trades near 107 now, roughly 28 percent below that post-deal level. The video shows a five-day green chart and omits that.

theses.title: Breadth ratio: equal-weight over cap-weight S&P as a regime signal
theses.structural_claim: The equal-weight S&P 500 divided by the cap-weighted S&P 500 (RSP over SPY) is called 'the equity market's real golden ratio'. Rising means breadth is broadening and more names are participating; falling means the market is narrowing into a few megacaps. The chart shown is RSP/SPY daily with 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages and a 14-day relative strength index, annotated 'Dominant broadening' at troughs and 'Countercycle narrowing' at peaks.
what_must_be_true: The breadth state has to FORECAST something, not merely describe concentration that already happened
It has to beat, or add to, the SPY 200-day gate Strategy C already uses, since that is the incumbent it would replace
The edge must survive at more than one parameter value, or it is a fitted artifact

load_bearing_claim.claim: The ratio is a usable regime signal, not just a description
load_bearing_claim.checked_against: breadth_gate.py, RSP and SPY daily 2003-2026, 5,878 sessions
load_bearing_claim.note: MECHANIZABLE, which is why it was worth testing at all: two liquid funds, a ratio and a moving average, every term defined. Unlike the session-sweep video there was something to falsify. Breadth is also a genuine professional measure, not an invention. It still did not hold up. As a FORECAST it is null: the spread in forward SPY returns between broadening and narrowing is -0.28%, -0.36% and -1.43% at one, three and twelve months on the 200-day version, all NEGATIVE and all tiny, across 161 independent regime episodes. As a GATE it is beaten by the incumbent: Strategy C's SPY-200-day gate returns 7.9% at Sharpe 0.72 with a -21% drawdown, while the breadth gate manages 6.6% at 0.64 with -24% and sits out half the time. Combining them with AND is worse still at 4.7%.

theses.marker_note: Opens with 'I'm reluctant to even share', which is a scarcity frame rather than evidence. No entry, exit or sizing. IMPORTANT READ LIMITATION: the reel had no captions and no Whisper key was configured, so it was read from frames alone and the caption fragments are incomplete. The phrase 'the first rule to use it' is visible but the rule that follows was not captured, so what was tested is the NATURAL reading of the indicator, not necessarily the creator's exact rule.
theses.expression_note: Not a stock tip. The two instruments are the indicator itself, and both are large liquid exchange-traded funds with ordinary access.

fund_check.headline: Rejected as a market-timing gate. Marginal at best as a rotation signal, and only at one of two parameters.
detail: The fairest version of the claim is rotation, not timing: a ratio of A over B is most naturally used to choose between A and B. Testing it only as a SPY gate would have been a strawman, so it was tested both ways.

Rotation (own RSP while broadening, SPY while narrowing) on the 50-day average returns 11.5% at Sharpe 0.67 against 10.7% and 0.64 for simply holding SPY, and beats a random rotation whose median Sharpe over 200 trials is 0.60. So there is a small apparent edge.

But the 200-day version returns 10.9% at Sharpe 0.64, which is identical to just holding SPY. An effect that appears at one parameter and vanishes at the other is the fitted-artifact signature, and the 50-day was chosen AFTER seeing both. Drawdown is also worse than holding SPY (-58% against -55%), so it buys nothing on the risk side.

Honest status: not established. The walk-forward harness built for the overnight rule is the tool that would settle it, and until that is run the 0.03 Sharpe margin is noise-level and should not move anything.
What the indicator IS good for is undisputed and worth keeping: it measures how concentrated the market is right now. That is a real description. The error is treating a thermometer as a forecast.
